|errata_history=This is the original printed text of [[Ben Solo]] (its only version). The image here is the Players Committee card image as first published. It is the current text. Each version below is quoted in full with its dated source. Every published image or slip that differs visibly from the one before is a version, numbered in release order; a printed errata mark that does not match that order is recorded as a PC transcription error (Bill, 12 November 2026). A same-words slip on a Players Committee release sheet that reprints a card image is part of that card image's version, not a version of its own (Bill, 17 November 2026).
* '''Original''' (this page): Players Committee card image first published 26 December 2024<ref name="ht-d64059d">Players Committee card image <code>Virtual24-Light/large/bensolo.gif</code> as published 26 December 2024: [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/holotable/d64059dd1b272bb73e7c5e8e8f001036fd2a5524/Images-HT/starwars/Virtual24-Light/large/bensolo.gif holotable commit d64059d] “Fixing case and making gifs” (the PC's card-image repository, which serves res.starwarsccg.org/cards).</ref>: “If drawn for destiny, may take Rey or a lightsaber into hand from Reserve Deck; reshuffle. Adds 3 to power of anything he pilots. Deploys only if an [Episode VII] Epic Event on table. Your total battle destiny here is +1 for each of your Interrupts out of play (limit +3). Once per game, may deploy a lightsaber on Ben from Lost Pile.”
*: This card image was also printed as a slip on the Players Committee's Virtual Set 24 release sheet<ref name="sheet24-20250202">Players Committee, [https://res.starwarsccg.org/virtual/Set-24.pdf Virtual Set 24 release sheet] (PDF, 3 pages, footer “SWCCG Players Committee, December 2024”; file created 2 February 2025). Released with [[Virtual Set 24]] (30 December 2024); the PDF is dated by its creation date.</ref>, page 2, file created 2 February 2025, under the label “•Ben Solo”. Same words ([[:File:V24-L-bensolo-2025-02-02-sheet-slip.png]]). Under the slip-and-composite rule (Bill, 17 November 2026) the slip is part of this version, not a version of its own.
